html:
The Warrgamay, also spelt Warakamai, are an Aboriginal Australian people of north Queensland, whose country is the lower Herbert River valley around today's Ingham.

Their neighbours were the Nyawaygi on the coast, the Dyirbal speakers of the rainforest and the Gugu Badhun up the river. The linguist R. M. W. Dixon recorded their language from its last speakers.

From the 1870s the Herbert valley was cleared for sugar cane, worked at first by Pacific Islanders brought in under the blackbirding labour trade.
